LIVE 2026 general, per precinct. 'Precinct Summary Report / INKOSG26', 242 pages, real text layer, 65 of 65 precincts reported. Sitting next to it as id=4299 is '2026 General Election Summary Results', the countywide report -- the labels differ by one word, so take 4300. validate_join.py places all 65 printed precincts (64 exact, 1 after dropping a city suffix: 'Plain 05 City Of Warsaw' -> 'PLAIN 05'). The geography has 69: three are marked (NV), no registered voters, which the EMS omits rather than printing zeros, and PRAIRIE 02 - WARSAW is a genuine unexplained gap. int(Precinct ID)*10 would 'match' all 65 codes and put 29 of them on the wrong precinct. Found via the eGov document center's `center.egov?view=all`, which lists every document a county holds and is the fastest way into an eGov site

LIVE 2026 general, per precinct. One PDF per precinct in a public Drive folder, each named for the precinct it reports -- Anderson.pdf, Boon 03.pdf, Ohio 19.pdf. All 53 filenames match a 2026 geography precinct exactly on the normalized name, bijectively, with nothing left over on either side; the join key is the filename itself. Checked Anderson.pdf: 'Precinct Summary Report / INWARG26', precinct 0101-ANDERSON, 388 ballots of 905 registered, E/A/W split. Drive's own folder page is virtualized and stops at 50 rows, which silently hides Owen, Pigeon and Skelton; list it through drive.google.com/embeddedfolderview?id=<folder> instead, which returns all 53 as plain HTML. Fetch a file with drive.google.com/uc?export=download&id=<id>, whose Content-Disposition carries the precinct name. The countywide file linked beside the folder is an ELECTION Summary Report -- the other half of the usual trap
